transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-10 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (NovaHealth CTO), Miguel Ramirez (Lead Eng), Lena Cho (PM)

[00:00] Ethan Moore: Hey team, thanks for joining, we want to keep this tight — 45 minutes — catch up on SDK integration and the structured output work. Priya's going to walk through the logs and the benchmark plan. Aisha, Miguel, Lena — good to see you.

[00:30] Aisha Patel: Thanks Ethan. Yep we have Miguel and Lena on. We've been testing the SDK wrapper you sent last week; quick note — we hit some serialization issues when the tool call returns nested arrays.

[01:10] Priya Singh: got it. When you say the SDK wrapper, is that the node example or the python one? We had slightly different shaped responses between them.

[01:30] Miguel Ramirez: We're using node in the app stack. The node example's fine for simple generative calls but when we do tool calls that return structured output — like a diagnosis object, list of medications — our validation layer chokes, expecting strict keys. Some fields come back as strings instead of arrays in a couple of cases.

[02:05] Ethan Moore: That sounds like a structured-output schema mismatch. Our SDK has a helper to coerce types but it was a beta path. Priya, can you remind them about the schema enforcement flag?

[02:25] Priya Singh: Sure — there's a parameter in the SDK client, schema_validation: true, which runs a lightweight JSON schema check on the model output. It's not enabled by default because it adds latency, but for POC we recommend turning it on. Also note we have the structuredOutput mode which wraps function/tool calls into deterministic envelopes: {"_type": "tool_result", "tool": "name", "payload": ... } — apologies if the auto-transcript says the name wrong — the format might've been transcribed as "tool pig" earlier in our internal docs.

[03:05] Lena Cho: If we enable schema_validation, how big is the latency hit? Our SLAs target <250ms 95p for the critical flows.

[03:30] Priya Singh: good question. On hosted small models it's about 10-20ms overhead. On dedicated GPUs with batching it's more variable — maybe 30-60ms depending on batch size and seq len. For your POC numbers Miguel sent earlier, you were averaging 180ms 95p; so adding schema validation still keeps you under 250ms in most cases. But the real impact shows up when function calls cascade.

[04:20] Miguel Ramirez: Cascading is exactly our problem. We call a primary model to parse user text then invoke multiple tool calls — one to lookup patient records, another to normalize meds, then a final summarization. The KV cache isn't helping there because each tool call resets context in our current impl. Is there a recommended pattern to keep context across tool/function calls?

[05:00] Priya Singh: yes — we recommend persistent prefix caching for those workflows. You can keep the conversation context and tool outputs in the KV cache and reference them with short keys — that avoids re-sending long history. There's a sample in the SDK under examples/persistent_cache.md. Small caveat: for privacy you may want to encrypt keys/fragments if you're using Private deployment with customer KMS — otherwise cache resides on Redwood side in hosted mode.

[05:45] Aisha Patel: We're leaning Private (VPC) for PHI concerns. How mature is the VPC onboarding? Miguel is worried about network egress, routing, and whether we can bring our KMS.

[06:10] Ethan Moore: VPC onboarding is a standard option on Redwood Private. You can bring your KMS/HSM; we support AWS KMS and common HSM flows. Priya will send the KMS integration guide. For egress — you can lock down egress via customer-managed NAT and we can support private endpoints. We'll include the SOC2/ISO pack in the next email.

[06:40] Miguel Ramirez: what about fallbacks? If dedicated capacity saturates and we get routed to hosted, how will our tool calls behave — any differences in invocation or output schemas?

[07:00] Priya Singh: functionally identical APIs. Small differences are in available model variants — e.g., we might route to a quantized variant with slightly different sampling behavior. For strict schema needs we recommend pinning model versions and adding validation; our canary policy can fallback to a compatible variant but we log model-version in the response so you can detect any drift.

[07:45] Lena Cho: We observed a sporadic tokenization mismatch — names with accents split differently, which causes downstream exact-match lookup failures. Any suggestions?

[08:10] Priya Singh: For tokenization we recommend normalizing inputs on your side (NFKC unicode normalization) and using exact_match:false in the lookup step, or canonicalization via a small deterministic post-process function. Also you can pass experimental tokenizer settings if you onboard model variant that supports it.

[08:50] Ethan Moore: quick pivot to SDK details — Miguel, can you confirm which SDK version you're on? The one we sent last week was 0.9.3-beta.

[09:05] Miguel Ramirez: We're on 0.9.2 — I think we missed the patch with the function-call schema fix.

[09:20] Ethan Moore: ok we'll push 0.9.3 stable to you today. That includes better typing for tool outputs and a helper to flatten nested arrays for the node client.

[09:40] Aisha Patel: Would that helper mutate the response or return a normalized copy? We need immutability in our pipelines.

[09:55] Priya Singh: returns a normalized copy by default; there's an option mutate:true if you want to avoid copy overhead. Default keeps your original object intact.

[10:15] Lena Cho: On structured output schemas — we shared an initial schema for the diagnosis object. There are a few optional fields that the model sometimes omits, causing our parser to fail. Can we make the SDK tolerant and include a schema migration strategy?

[10:45] Priya Singh: absolutely — we support schema versions: include schema_version in the tool manifest and the SDK will run a migration step if a known older version is detected. For unknown shapes you can enable a soft_fail: true flag that returns validation warnings rather than throwing. That lets you log mismatches without breaking the pipeline.

[11:20] Miguel Ramirez: That would be ideal — we can log and alert on mismatches and then iterate. Also curious about cost — function calls increase per-token and per-invocation metrics. If we move to dedicated, can we estimate unit cost delta?

[11:40] Ethan Moore: dedicated is charged by reserved capacity vs hosted per-token. For your expected scale (Miguel's spreadsheet: ~200k tokens/day, spikes to 1M tokens/day) dedicated starts to be more cost-effective around that spike profile. We'll send a cost model comparing hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved pool with estimated batching gains.

[12:15] Aisha Patel: Please include a scenario where we aggressively batch tool calls — Miguel wants to batch the three internal tool calls into one multiplexed call if possible. Is that supported?

[12:35] Priya Singh: you can multiplex calls in a single request by using the multi-tool call pattern the SDK exposes; it's experimental in 0.9.x but supported. There's a batching guide that shows when multiplexing helps vs when it hurts because of longer max seq lengths. We'll share the tradeoff doc.

[13:10] Ethan Moore: let's look at the preliminary benchmark that Priya ran — Priya over to you for the numbers you uploaded to the shared spreadsheet.

[13:25] Priya Singh: sure — I ran three 2-hour windows on a dedicated staging cluster with the model variant you requested. 95p latency was ~170ms with batch size 8, cost per 1k tokens basement was X (see sheet), and with schema_validation on we saw +40ms. Under multiplexing the 95p rose to 240ms because of longer sequences, though median stayed low. Note — I saw a couple of error spikes at 03:40 UTC due to a background rebalancing event in the cluster; I marked them in the logs as probably noise.

[14:20] Miguel Ramirez: that +40ms is acceptable. Are the logs downloadable in structured format? We need per-request model-version, route, and token counts to attribute cost.

[14:40] Priya Singh: yes — Redwood Console exposes per-request traces and you can export to csv/json. I'll include a link to the trace export for the 24h run once we do the longer benchmark.

[15:00] Lena Cho: About error handling — if a tool call fails, do you recommend retrying idempotently or fallback to a summarization-only path? We want deterministic user experiences.

[15:20] Priya Singh: Retry idempotently for transient errors up to n=2 with exponential backoff; after that a graceful degradation path is recommended — like return partial data with a warning in the structured output envelope. We can add a "tool_status" field to responses so your UI can show degraded states.

[16:00] Aisha Patel: Good. On security, Miguel asked whether logs can be encrypted at rest and whether audit logs include token-level info.

[16:20] Ethan Moore: Yes — in Private mode we support customer-managed KMS for encrypting logs and KV cache. Audit logs include request IDs, model-version, timestamps, and non-sensitive metadata. We don't persist user inputs for hosted trial accounts by default unless you opt-in in the config. We'll send the exact retention and fields table.

[17:00] Miguel Ramirez: One more thing — when tool calls return attachments (like PDF extracts), how does the SDK handle binary blobs?

[17:20] Priya Singh: SDK returns a signed URL by default for large objects; you can also opt to inline base64 payloads but that's not recommended for large binaries. We also support a presignedness TTL param.

[18:00] Ethan Moore: let's talk routing and fallback policies briefly — once you move to Dedicated, you can set burst policies that allow routing to hosted when reserved capacity is saturated; we recommend a soft-fallback route with model-version pinning.

[18:30] Lena Cho: We'll need clear observability — per-route, per-model dashboards and alerts on token cost and latency. Does Redwood Console let us set alert thresholds on 95p latency?

[18:50] Priya Singh: yes — thresholds, tracing hooks, and per-API-key cost allocations exist. You can create an alert that ties to a Slack webhook.

[19:10] Miguel Ramirez: For the POC we want a simple pass/fail for structured output correctness and performance thresholds. Can we get a smoke test script?

[19:30] Priya Singh: we have a smoke-test repo with node/python tests that run a small set of prompts and validate schema. We'll share a customized script for your diagnosis schema.

[20:00] Ethan Moore: quick check — are there any blockers that would prevent Miguel's team from running the 24-hour benchmark this week?

[20:10] Miguel Ramirez: only blocker is getting the updated SDK and the staging creds with dedicated pool access.

[20:25] Ethan Moore: we will provide an updated SDK and staging creds today. Priya, you'll run the longer benchmark from Redwood side as well, and we'll compare.

[20:40] Priya Singh: yes I'll schedule a 24-hour run tonight and share results tomorrow morning. Also I'll enable deeper logging on rebalancing to avoid that noise.

[21:05] Aisha Patel: Timeline-wise — if all goes well we want to evaluate security pack and cost model and decide by end of next week whether to pilot Private.

[21:20] Ethan Moore: sounds good. Last thing — any competitor concerns? I heard you trialed Anthropic on a gen task earlier, any specific gaps?

[21:35] Miguel Ramirez: We liked Anthropic for some safety aspects but the latency was a hair worse and integration hooks were less mature. OpenAI was fast but cost was higher. Replicate had good self-host flexibility but lacked enterprise-grade telemetry. Those are all tradeoffs we weighed.

[22:10] Lena Cho: ok let's recap next steps — send SDK 0.9.3, staging creds, security pack, run 24h benchmark, provide traffic profile.

[22:30] Ethan Moore: recap: Ethan send SDK + security docs; Priya run bench + share logs; Miguel provide traffic profile + run local bench; NovaHealth schedule failover test window.

[22:50] Aisha Patel: thanks all, we'll aim to have the traffic profile to you by Friday.

[23:05] Ethan Moore: great, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set a short 20-minute check next Wednesday. Thanks everyone.

[23:20] End meeting.

Notes: transcript contains a few auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., "tool pig" instead of tool name, "K-V cash" instead of KV cache). Links referenced during call: shared spreadsheet (link omitted), SDK repo (link omitted), security pack (link to be sent).
